title: Sosulski et al. 2019 — Online Optimization of Stimulation Speed in an Auditory Brain-Computer Interface under Time Constraints
description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an auditory oddball (P300) paradigm with 1000 Hz target and 500 Hz non-target tones at varying stimulus onset asynchronies (60-600 ms). The data were collected to evaluate closed-loop Bayesian optimization and random search for selecting individually optimal stimulation speed in an auditory brain-computer interface. The dataset contains an optimization part and a validation part, recorded with 31 EEG channels at 1000 Hz.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz with a BrainProducts BrainAmp DC amplifier using passive Ag/AgCl electrodes and nose reference. Each trial had 15 target and 75 non-target tones. The optimization part used four strategies (AUC-ucb, AUC-rand, P300-ucb, P300-rand), each allotted 20 minutes. The validation part tested the selected SOAs and a fixed 60 ms SOA for 20 trials each. Features were mean amplitudes in 5 time intervals across channels, classified with shrinkage-regularized LDA and 13-fold cross-validation.
